- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; adjust downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- Overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., 35.94 → 36.62) — cap forecast peaks at 10–15% above recent high to avoid overreaction.
- Mean reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect downward after spikes; add 2–3% upward adjustment in mid-horizon if recent price > 35.
- Sentiment history is flat (0.00) in all examples — no sentiment-driven correction needed; model should not react to sentiment unless sentiment > 0.20.
- Horizon-specific: last 3–5 days of forecast often lag behind true outcome; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead for final 5–7 days to capture momentum.
- Avoid “sudden drop” pattern: if true outcome shows sharp decline after spike, model should not predict further drop — instead, assume stabilization or slight rebound.
